business: Air Force One Plumbing Heating & Air, now part of A-Star Air Conditioning & Plumbng
text:
This is a mixed review. On the one hand, ownership of Air Force One was responsive when one of their techs mishandled the AC system in my attic causing a ceiling to flood. I hired Air Force One to perform a deep cleaning and coolant check of my HVAC system in Fall 2021. The tech pointed out there was rust in the old overflow pan, but he did not check for leaks after he removed/reinstalled the original pan. I told him that I would make plans to replace the pan in the winter when it was cooler to work in the attic. The tech thought that was a good idea. Due to the way the tech handled the old drain pan, the pan leaked and flooded the ceiling of the bedroom directly below the unit in the attic. I was beyond angry and, in all honesty, expected a typical "it's not our fault" response from Air Force One.

I was happy and impressed when the manager of Air Force One came to my house to inspect the damage and the leaking drain pan early the next morning. He apologized sincerely and promptly sent a repairman who replaced the ceiling and painted. The replacement ceiling seems to have been installed properly, but the paint had numerous spots where it did not properly cover the new ceiling. When I called the manager of Air Force One he came to my house, agreed with my assessment and sent the repairman back to fix the mistakes. Air Force One also replaced the overflow pan that their employee broke. Everyone makes a mistake from time to time so I was very satisfied with the way Air Force One handled the problems that they created.

Until last week... My AC stopped working and the system shut down. I contacted Air Force One management via text message and did not receive a reply after waiting a day so I contacted another repairman. What the new repairman found is that Air Force One a) connected the cut-off float in the new drain pan incorrectly so it shut down the entire system (should have shut the AC down and left the fan running), b) they installed sheet metal screws at the rear of the new drain pain at the very bottom of the pan which was already leaking, c) connected the wires from the thermostat incorrectly on the attic AC unit, d) did not install the drain pipe from the rear of the overflow pan that they installed which stopped the water from draining and made it overflow again (thank goodness it did not destroy the ceiling this time - I guess the extreme heat in the attic evaporated the water before it could saturate the ceiling again) and e) reversed the wires on the outside compressor so the exhaust fan was blowing down into the compressor and condenser coil instead of blowing up/out of the unit. There were a couple more mistakes & oversights, but these are the highlights.

Air Force One has many happy customers and that's why I called them in the first place. After my experience last week where I had to pay another company to replace the brand new drain pain, properly align the drain pipe so it actually drains and rewire the entire system - inside and out - I will not use Air Force One again. That's a shame because they are nice people.

text: Dont use this company in a commercial setting, (unless you have some money to burn.)  We had used this company for years in a commercial building.  They recently changed hands to a new owner.  They didnt come out to do our regularly scheduled quarterly maintenance.   Then we moved to a new commercial building that we bought.  The air conditioning unit that we were using for the office stopped cooling, so we called Air Force one to trouble shoot; Sam came out and told us that we could replace some parts; compressors, evaporator coils, etc, & said that the estimate would be $4-6K.  We never got the estimate.  After stating that they couldnt get the parts, Sam said that we could buy the parts, and they 'might' install them, and that LABOR ONLY would be $6-7K.  Or we could buy a new unit for $14K and they could install it in 2 days.  So I called my friend who runs a BIG HVAC company (they do Amazon warehouses all over the US).  They pulled a service tech off of an Amazon job in north Ft Worth.  He crawled up on the roof, and had our unit running in less than 1 hr.  The only thing that was wrong was a bad capacitor (which is like a battery)... a $100 part.  These crooks were trying to fleece us of $14,000 when all they needed to do was replace a $100 part.  I spoke to the owner, Josh, who acted horrified.  I dont know what more embarrassing for him- the fact that they were trying to push a new unit for $14K, or the fact that his service tech didnt know how to identify a faulty $100 capacitor.   And he is running his business out of his house?  Go with a real professional company who has their own place of business, and techs that know what they are doing.

Review of Dunrite Heating & Cooling

I’ve used Dunrite in the past and previously appreciated their professionalism and quality service. Unfortunately, my most recent experience has fallen far short of that standard.

In April, during a routine A/C inspection, Dunrite reported that everything was functioning well. However, during a subsequent home inspection as I prepared to sell my home, a separate inspector noted an A/C issue. I asked Dunrite to take a closer look, and they then discovered a failed compressor. Given my circumstances, I made it clear that I wanted to invest minimally. Despite this, they strongly recommended replacing the entire unit, citing warranty issues and parts availability.

Ultimately, I opted to replace just the part—at a cost of over $6,000. I was told someone would contact me to schedule installation, but no one did. I followed up, only to find out I was already on the schedule without having been notified. The part was eventually installed—but the issues continued.

Within two weeks, my downstairs unit wasn't cooling properly. The thermostat was set to 76°F, yet indoor temps exceeded 80°F. I called Dunrite again and requested a follow-up inspection at no charge. The technician who came was professional and helpful—he diagnosed a leaking coil and offered to reduce the cost by charging only for labor. I appreciated this gesture and proceeded, though it still cost over $3,000.

Once again, I was told I’d be contacted for scheduling. This time I did receive a call, but it was last-minute—fortunately my work schedule was flexible, but that may not be the case for everyone. The team arrived and successfully completed the fix.

Then, to my surprise, my upstairs unit started overheating just 24–48 hours later. Dunrite came out and diagnosed the same issue as the downstairs unit—another leaking coil—along with recommendations to replace three parts totaling over $12,000. That number was shocking, so I opted to replace just the coil at a cost of over $6,000.

Unfortunately, the same scheduling missteps happened again. I wasn’t contacted to confirm a time until I called, only to learn I was already on the schedule. I asked that they come after a critical work call—yet during that call, I received calls and texts from their team saying no one would be arriving and I’d be rescheduled for 8 a.m. the next day.

The following day, no one arrived by 9 a.m., so I followed up. I was told they’d likely be there by 9:30. That time came and went, and by noon I learned the part had been sent to the wrong location, which was closed for the holiday weekend.

I requested a partial refund so I could pursue service elsewhere. I was placed on hold repeatedly and told a manager would contact me—no one did. After the holiday weekend, no technician showed up first thing Tuesday morning as promised, and again I had to follow up myself. I asked to speak to a manager and was routed to a voicemail. No return call.
In summary:

Communication is severely lacking—I had to follow up repeatedly to get basic updates.

Customer experience does not seem to be a priority.

Pricing is inconsistent, with significant fluctuations for similar repairs.

Escalation handling is ineffective—promised manager callbacks never happened.

To be fair, Dunrite's technicians are knowledgeable, and they do provide thorough inspection reports. But this experience has been frustrating, costly, and time-consuming—and left me feeling unsupported throughout the process.

Regretfully, I cannot recommend Dunrite at this time.
